newsitem.title: UK: Monthly Review - Peru siege dominates in December.
newsitem.headline: Monthly Review - Peru siege dominates in December.

text.p: Opposition rallies in Serbia and a standoff between Peruvian authorities and Marxist rebels holding hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima dominated the news in December.

Guerrillas from the Peruvian Tupac Amaru group seized 490 hostages, including ambassadors and ministers. By the end of the month they were still holding 81 and demanding the release of jailed comrades.

In Belgrade, tens of thousands demonstrated through the month against President Slobodan Milosovic, accusing him of falsifying election results to retain his hold on power. An OSCE report backed opposition claims that they had won local polls in key cities.
Here is a chronology of the main events of the month:
Dec 2 - Suspected Kashmiri militants bomb a train near Chandigarh, Punjab, killing 12 and injuring 37.
Dec 3 - Four people are killed and over 90 injured when an explosion rocks an underground station in Paris.
Dec 3 - Zairean rebels capture the northeastern town of Bunia and Walikale to the west.
Dec 4 - NASA's first Mars Pathfinder takes off from Cape Canaveral. It is due to reach Mars on July 4, 1997.
Dec 5 - Two-day review conference on Bosnia ends with a warning to Bosnian leaders that future aid depends on their full compliance with the Dayton peace accords.
Dec 7 - Algerian President Liamine Zeroual signs into law constitutional reforms which ban political parties based on religion or language.
Dec 7 - Latin American summit approves a 65-point declaration on the environment and economic development.
Dec 7 - Jerry Rawlings becomes the first incumbent president of Ghana to be re-elected since independence in 1957.
Dec 8 - Belgrade's electoral commission awards victory in local elections to Serbia's ruling parties despite opposition claims of fraud.

Dec 9 - The United Nations authorises a long-delayed "oil-for-food" deal with Iraq. The next day President Saddam Hussein presses the button to start Iraqi oil flowing to world markets for the first time since 1990.
Dec 10 - President Nelson Mandela signs South Africa's post- apartheid constitution into law.
Dec 11 - Shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa is selected by a Beijing-backed body as Hong Kong's leader-in-waiting; China formally endorses him the next day.
Dec 12 - Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday is shot and wounded while driving in Baghdad.
Dec 13 - Ministers from 128 nations sign a series of ground-breaking agreements at the inaugural conference of the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
Dec 14 - European Union leaders agree on a landmark pact on budget discipline and a new Exchange Rate Mechanism.
Dec 15 - Up to 250,000 protesters demonstrate in Belgrade against Serbian President Milosevic's handling of local elections, the biggest rally in a series of protests.
Dec 15 - Boeing and McDonnell Douglas announce a merger to form the world's largest aerospace company.
Dec 15 - Hundreds of thousands of Rwandan refugees begin returning home after a two-and-a-half year exile in Tanzania.
Dec 16 - Israel and the Palestinians agree after U.S. intervention to resume talks on an Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron.
Dec 16 - A South Korean appeals court commutes the death sentence on ex-president Chun Doo Hwan to life imprisonment.
Dec 16 - A former Daiwa Bank Ltd. bond trader is sentenced to four years in prison and fined $2 million for conspiring to hide $1.1 billion in losses.
Dec 17 - Six Western staff members of the International Committee of the Red Cross are shot dead in the rebel Russian region of Chechnya.
Dec 17 - Zaire's veteran president, Mobutu Sese Seko, returns home to reassert power and combat a rebellion in the east after four months in Europe undergoing treatment for prostate cancer.
Dec 17 - U.N. General Assembly appoints Kofi Annan of Ghana to a five-year term as secretary-general, beginning Jan 1.
Dec 17 - A supertanker laden with Iraqi crude oil leaves an Iraqi port for the first time in six years.
Dec 17 - Peruvian rebels storm the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima, threatening to kill almost 490 hostages unless the government frees jailed comrades.
Dec 18 - FBI arrests its own agent, Earl Edwin Pitts, on charges of selling security secrets to Russia since 1987.
Dec 20 - NATO commanders formally launch a new multinational peacekeeping mission in Bosnia.
Dec 23 - The warring sides in Tajikistan's bitter four-year civil war sign two key accords aimed at securing peace in the former Soviet republic.
Dec 24 - A German woman detonates grenades in a Frankfurt church killing herself and two others. Thirteen people are seriously injured.
Dec 26 - Strikes begin in South Korea after the government pushes through a labour law at a clandestine dawn session of the National Assembly along with 10 other bills.
Dec 27 - Anti-government demonstrators and riot police clash after a protest rally in Belgrade and an OSCE report backs Serbian opposition claims it was robbed of election victories.
Dec 27 - Rwanda's first genocide trial opens with the accused facing the death penalty if convicted of taking part in the slaughter in 1994 of some 800,000 Tutsis.
Dec 27 - Russian President Boris Yeltsin meets visiting Chinese Premier Li Peng, his first meeting with a foreign leader since a heart operation in November.
Dec 29 - Guatemala's government and leftist rebels sign a peace accord ending 36 years of war that cost at least 140,000 lives.
Dec 30 - The bodies of 24 North Korean intruders shot in South Korea are handed back after Pyongyang apologises for an incursion by their submarine in September.
Dec 30 - A crowded train is blown up in India's northeastern state of Assam. Authorities, who blame separatist t Bodo tribal guerrillas, expect the death toll to rise from the 59 bodies found so far.

Deaths in December include: Babrak Karmal, former communist leader of Afghanistan (Dec 3); Jose Donoso, Chilean novelist (7); Mary Leakey, fossil hunter and mother of Richard Leakey (9); Marie-Claude Vaillant-Couturier, World War Two Resistance figure (11); Laurens van der Post, South African explorer and writer (15).

Sun Yaoting, China's last imperial eunuch (17); Marcello Mastroianni, Italian actor (19); Carl Sagan, U.S. astronomer and Pulitzer Prize-winning author (20); Ronnie Scott, British jazz saxophonist (23); Mireille, composer of popular French songs (29).
